newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle called steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle called steady to higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.500 cent higher after Friday's USDA monthly Cattle-on-Feed report, and feeder cattle were called steady to 0.200 higher, livestock analysts said.

Friday's cattle report was considered mildly bullish as August 1 on-feed numbers at seven-state major feedlots totaled 86 per cent of last year, as expected, and placements were at 106 percent versus the average estimate of 110.5 percent, analysts said.
The report was most bullish to December with daily fundamentals likely to limit gains in October, they said.

Fed cattle trade is expected to be very slow this week as packers have adequate live supplies following a record feedlot movement last week. Lower boxed beef values will also weigh on sentiment in October, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to show some spillover support from live cattle. The report shows there are more feeders available on grass that could be put onto feed and this will limit upside potential. Higher corn futures indications may also offset a higher index, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.11 at $63.20 per cwt.
